item.title: Portrait Cut for Two Speakers

turns.text: Turn this into a 9:16 vertical clip. Show the man when he asks his question, then the woman when she answers, with each centred while talking. Keep all 10 seconds and the original audio. No captions.

item.tests: Tests speaker-aware portrait reframing of a two-person conversation without losing either speaking turn.

answer_sheet.Source and speakers: Use talk-two.mp4. The man asks the question and the woman answers.
answer_sheet.Layout and transitions: Centre the current speaker in a full-frame portrait crop; a clean cut at the speaker change is fine.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, all 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Audio and text: Preserve the original conversation and sound, with no captions or added text.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 portrait edit of the attached office conversation.
The man is centred and his face is fully visible during his question.
The woman is centred and her face is fully visible during her answer.
Both speaking turns remain in their original order, with the full 10 seconds and original audio in sync.
The image is not stretched and contains no added captions.

turns.text: Could you turn this clip into a vertical version for me? I’m a little worried about how the conversation will look when it’s cropped. What I mean is, show the man when he asks his question, and make it 9:16, then show the woman when she answers. Please keep each person centred while they’re talking, since that’s the framing I’m trying to describe. Keep all 10 seconds and the original audio. I don’t want any captions.

dialog.agent:
You’re describing **speaker-following reframing**: a 9:16 crop centred on the man during his question, then a cut to a crop centred on the woman during her answer—with all 10 seconds, the original audio, and no captions.

I can’t reliably make that exact edit with the connected Magic Hour tools. They offer generative video editing, but no precise crop-and-cut controls or guaranteed preservation of the original audio. I don’t want to regenerate your conversation when you only want the framing changed.

In a standard video editor, the edit would be:
1. Set the canvas to **9:16**.
2. Keep the full clip and original audio unchanged.
3. Split only the picture where the woman starts answering.
4. Reposition each segment to centre the current speaker; add position keyframes if they move.
5. Export without captions.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

turns.agent:
Magic Hour refused the attempt because your account doesn’t have enough credits for this edit—even at the free-plan 480p setting. No video was generated.

You’d need additional credits to try it through Magic Hour. For this particular edit, a standard video editor would also give you more reliable speaker-centred cropping while preserving the original audio exactly.

approvals.name: edit_video

style.prompt: Reframe this existing conversation into a vertical 9:16 portrait video. Keep the entire original 10 seconds in original chronological order and preserve the original audio, dialogue, voices, timing and synchronization unchanged. This is a crop-and-reframe edit, not a new scene: preserve the original people, faces, expressions, mouth movements, clothing, setting, lighting and actions. During the man's question, crop to the man and keep him centred in the portrait frame. At the actual speaker change, cut to a portrait crop centred on the woman for her answer. Follow each speaker subtly if they move so the person speaking remains centred, with natural headroom. Do not use a fixed two-person crop, split screen or letterboxing. Do not add captions, subtitles, text, graphics, music, sound effects, new speech or any extra content. Output the full 10-second conversation as a 9:16 vertical video with its original audio.
